messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-api-us-east-1 queue depth > 50k for 3m, p95 latency spike detected. autoscale attempts failing (see logs). triggering P1 pager.

alice (oncall): @here I'm on it. seeing a big backlog on hosted-inference queue. p95 ~ 5.2s, p99 ~ 28s, 5xx climb to 7%. traffic spike looks organic from a partner integration.

ben (sre): grabbing metrics dashboard. GPU pool us-east-1 shows 99-100% utilization across all pools. Pending pods queued for node provisioning: 42. autoscaler events show repeated failures for new node launches.

caitlin (infra): checking cloud quotas now. quick note: provider returned quota_error on recent node requests. suspect we've hit GPU quota for the account/region.

maria (prod-eng): customer impact? any external timeouts/error pages? support seeing elevated error rates from customers.

alice (oncall): support flagged multiple 504s from several customers. lowest tier (free) traffic is majority of queue. higher tiers still getting degraded responses.

ben (sre): copy — logs snippet:
```
autoscaler: request node xla-gpu-8 failed -> 403 quota_exceeded: GPU quota 48/48 reached
autoscaler: retrying launch, backoff 30s
api-request: enqueue: 124,512 total pending
```

caitlin (infra): confirmed. cloud quota shows '0 spare' for nvidia-a100 in us-east-1. Recent bulk provisioning for a partner test consumed burst capacity earlier today.

maria (prod-eng): okay we need live mitigation — options: 1) enable fallback routing to smaller quantized models (lower GPU footprint), 2) drop or rate-limit free-tier traffic, 3) failover to secondary region (latency hit), 4) ask cloud to temporarily raise quota (slow).

alice (oncall): priority: reduce customer-impacting timeouts ASAP. actioning (2) and (1) in parallel. @caitlin can you attempt immediate quota raise with provider support and open emergency request?

caitlin (infra): opening ticket now and calling provider on emergency line. ETA unknown but I'll escalate.

ben (sre): implementing fallback routing now. patching routing table to prefer quantized-medium models for new requests and serve high-tier customers with reserved capacity.

deploy-bot: deploy started: route-update-fallback-20260315 -> canary on hosted-api (10% traffic) at commit abc123

alice (oncall): enabling soft rate limit for free tier: 100rps -> 20rps. this will shed noisy traffic and free up queue processing.

maria (prod-eng): listing customers to notify: partner-acme (heavy), partner-bento (medium), a few enterprise customers experiencing latency. I'll prepare a status note once we have more details.

ben (sre): canary looks stable. quantized-medium throughput ~2.5x per-GPU for short contexts (less perf on quality). routing change in flight: rolling to 30%.

alice (oncall): queue depth has started to drop from 124k -> 80k after rate limits and initial routing. p95 down to 2.1s, p99 12s. error rate trending down.

caitlin (infra): provider support responded: temporary quota increase request submitted, status pending human review. also found 6 idle reserved nodes in another project; opening cross-team ask to release.

maria (prod-eng): good call on reserved nodes, reaching out to team that owns 'research-batches' to release 4 nodes for 2 hours.

ben (sre): note: autoscaler logs show repeated create failures because cloud API returns 429 rate_limit on node creation attempts. adding exponential backoff and avoiding thundering herd.

alice (oncall): also enabling secondary-region failover for non-latency-sensitive requests. route ~10% to us-west-2. this will add network latency but prevents further timeouts for long polls.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: route-update-fallback-20260315 -> success

alice (oncall): current numbers: pending 38k, p95 1.4s, p99 6.8s, 5xx 1.7%. still some long tail but improving. keeping P1.

ben (sre): mitigation checklist:
- [x] soft rate limit free-tier
- [x] fallback routing to quantized-medium
- [x] avoid autoscaler thundering herd
- [ ] provider quota increase (in progress)
- [ ] release reserved nodes (in progress)
- [x] secondary-region failover enabled

caitlin (infra): provider escalated to on-call engineer. they asked to confirm exact SKU and region; response time ~15-30m. also requested we avoid additional node create requests to prevent hitting rate limits.

alice (oncall): noted — we'll halt further autoscaler retries and rely on routing/fallbacks. @maria keep customer comms ready.

maria (prod-eng): drafting status update: summary + actions + ETA. will post to status.redwood.com once we confirm full recovery.

ben (sre): small ops note — we observed one worker pool had a zombie process holding GPU locks leading to underutilized capacity estimation. will follow postmortem.

alice (oncall): handing off to night oncall @ben in 40m. leaving incident as P1 until quota/reserved nodes resolved. playbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hosted-queue-gpu-exhaust

ben (sre): acknowledged. I'll monitor for next 2h and coordinate with infra on quota updates.

caitlin (infra): provider confirmed temporary +8 GPUs for our account (provisional) — provisioning now. ETA 6m.

alice (oncall): great. queue at 12k now. p95 0.9s, p99 2.8s, 5xx 0.6%. looks like recovery path is working.

maria (prod-eng): posting preliminary status update to customers now. includes mitigation steps and expected follow-up.

ben (sre): follow-ups for postmortem:
- autoscaler retry/backoff tuning
- pre-warming reserve pool for peak windows
- quota-monitoring alerting (predictive)
- policy for rapid release of reserved nodes across teams
- investigate zombie GPU lock

alice (oncall): logging timeline and notes in incident tracker. handing incident fully to @ben at 1862349123.

pager-duty-bot: Incident acknowledged by ben (sre). P1 -> active. Handoff recorded.

ben (sre): taking it from here. will close incident when queue <100 and p99 <1s for 30m and provider quota status stabilized. leaving a note for postmortem invite.
